deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Grothendieck has a category E = E_M of 'tame' (modérés) spaces built from a system M = (M_n) of admissible subsets of R^n. In modern terms this is close to a category of definable sets in an o-minimal-type structure, with tame maps defined as maps whose graph is tame. He is studying when colimits exist in E and commute with the forgetful functor X -> |X| to Sets. The previous page gave a criterion for pushouts X_1 ⊔_Z X_2: the existence of a finite family of tame functions to R that separates points compatibly. Its NB generalised this to finite inductive systems: the quotient tame structure on X = colim |X_i| exists iff a finite compatible family of tame functions embeds X into R^A.

This page proves the universal property. Hypotheses: the set-theoretic colimit X of a (finite) inductive system (X_i) carries a tame structure, with maps g_i: X_i -> X, such that |X| is the union of the images g_i(X_i). Let Y be a tame space. A compatible family (f_i: X_i -> Y) is the same thing as a set map f: X -> Y with every f∘g_i tame. It therefore suffices to show that f is tame, i.e. that its graph Γ_f ⊂ X×Y is a tame subset. Since X is the union of the g_i(X_i), Γ_f is the union of the images of the graphs Γ_{f_i} ⊂ X_i×Y under the maps g_i×id_Y. Images of tame sets under tame maps are tame, and finite unions of tame sets are tame, so Γ_f is tame. Hence X is the colimit in E, and the forgetful functor commutes with it.

Corollary. Let f: X -> Y be tame. Its kernel equivalence relation R_f = X ×_Y X is a tame subset of X×X, and it is an E-equivalence relation. Then the quotient X/R_f exists in E and is canonically isomorphic to f(X) with the induced structure. The reason: f(X) is tame, being the image of a tame map. A tame map g: X -> Z that is constant on the fibres of f factors through f(X) by a map whose graph is the image of Γ_g under f×id, which is tame.

A second corollary, on cokernels of pairs X_1 ⇉ X_2 in E, is begun and then struck out. The next page introduces axioms (M6), contraction of a subspace to a point via finitely many tame functions, and (M7), extension of tame functions from a tame subspace. Together with (M5) these guarantee the existence of pushouts along tame embeddings.
errors: The argument needs the index set I to be finite, or at least the union of images to be a finite union, for Γ_f to be tame; this is implicit from the previous page ('famille finie') but not stated here.
Uses without comment that images of tame sets under tame maps are tame; this is fine for o-minimal-type axioms but is an axiom or lemma, not automatic.

In the corollary, effectivity is trivial because f(X) is already an object of E. The real content of quotient existence (general tame equivalence relations, as in o-minimal definable choice / elimination of imaginaries) is not addressed here.

ideas.what: Colimits in the category of tame spaces exist and commute with the forgetful functor once the set-theoretic colimit carries a tame structure covered by the images; proved via graphs being finite unions of images of graphs
ideas.modern_name: finite colimits / gluing in the category of definable sets (o-minimal 'definable spaces')
ideas.usually_credited_to: van den Dries (Tame topology and o-minimal structures, 1998, ch. 10 on definable spaces and quotients); Pillay; Shiota
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 discusses tame topology and the need for quotients/contractions in general terms, without this lemma

ideas.what: Quotient of a tame space by the kernel equivalence relation of a tame map exists and equals the image with induced structure
ideas.modern_name: definable image; effective kernel-pair quotient in the category of definable sets

deep.surprise_reason: A routine categorical verification (colimit universal property via graphs) and a trivial corollary (image as quotient), inside Grothendieck's axiomatic tame-topology programme. The programme itself is known from the Esquisse, and these facts are standard in o-minimal geometry.
transcription_corrections: 'ce qui est[?] le domaine d'une relation[?] f : X → Y' should read approximately 'ce qui équivaut à la donnée d'une application f : X → Y'.
'Il est évident[?] : prouver que' is more likely 'Il suffit donc de prouver que'.
'une [-Syst.-] limite des syst. inductif' is probably 'un morphisme du syst. inductif (X_i) (dans E) dans Y' (uncertain).
'E = E_mod[?]' looks like 'E = E_M' (subscripted M, i.e. E_{M_n}), consistent with the next page.
Struck-out 'Cor. 2 Conditions ... X_1 ⇉ X_2' appears to concern cokernels of a double arrow 'dans E'.
